sections.h2: What should a seller know about Paulding County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Paulding County is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta, with Dallas as the county seat and the county government campus on Constitution Boulevard. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 190,996 people, a 13.3 percent gain on the 168,630 in its 2020 base. That is the largest population of the four Georgia counties in this comparison, packed into 312.35 square miles of land.

The housing numbers explain why sales here move at a different pace than in rural south Georgia. Typical home value, for 2020 to 2024, is $326,300, and four in five dwellings (80.8 percent) are lived in by their owners. The county issued 1,326 building permits in 2025, and the median gross rent was $1,772. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, a sign that many residents commute toward Atlanta.

For a seller, the tax side is simple in outline. Value is fixed on January 1, taxed at 40 percent of that figure, and the commissioner multiplies by the millage. The commissioner's general information page explains the sequence. What follows concentrates on points that come up when a Paulding County house is sold.

sections.h2: Which Paulding County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work, and a third handles deeds. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Paulding County property tax offices, as listed on the county websites

The commissioner's page warns that the phone line may be cut off early so the office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email at the address printed on the county's homestead page, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

sections.h2: When is Paulding County property tax due, and what does a late bill cost?
sections.html:
On the commissioner's general information page, the deadline is November 15 every year. An FAQ page elsewhere on that site still lists a December 4 date for tax year 2024, so use the date on your own bill when you plan a payoff or pick a closing day.

The general information page spells out what happens after the deadline:

  • Interest posts to the account on the 16th of every month, calculated as prime plus 3 percent spread over twelve months.
  • A lien filing (the county uses the term FIFA) goes on record with the Clerk of Superior Court a month after the delinquent notice is dated.
  • Penalties of 5 percent land at the 120-day mark and recur on that cycle until they reach 20 percent in total.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. Bills usually go out near January 2 and fall due April 1, and a 10 percent penalty follows on April 2.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Paulding County assessment?
sections.html:
The clock is 45 days, counted from the day the assessment notice was mailed, and the county says nothing can be filed once it runs out. Grounds are limited to whether the parcel is taxable, what it is worth and whether that value is fair next to similar homes. Anger about the millage or the total on the bill will not carry an appeal.

The path through the system runs in a fixed order:

  • File the appeal with the Board of Assessors, which reviews its own value and tells you what it decided.
  • Without a deal at that stage, the file moves up to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Arbitration is the alternative to that board, and the assessors' staff can walk you through it.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form, a 2026 guide to reading the notice, and a list of 2025 sales used for comparison. When an owner is away on military duty, a friend or relative may file within 90 days of the value notice. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions can a Paulding County owner claim?
sections.html:
A Paulding County homeowner must apply with the Board of Assessors, because exemptions are never granted automatically. Expect to show residency and citizenship papers, for example a Georgia license or ID card, and your name has to be on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

The county's homestead page names several categories beyond the standard exemption:

  • Lower school tax for owners aged 65 or more.
  • Relief for owners with a total and permanent disability.
  • A break for veterans rated fully disabled from service.
  • Relief for the widow or widower of a peace officer or firefighter who died on duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. The assessors say applications must arrive by April 1, while the homestead page ties the current-year deadline to the appeal deadline on that year's assessment notice, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Preferential programs for farmland and timber require a covenant of at least 10 years.

sections.h2: What happens to Paulding County property tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Dividing the year's tax between buyer and seller is a contract term, and your closing attorney puts the numbers on the settlement statement.

Request a balance figure from the commissioner before the sign goes up, including any interest, penalty or lien recorded against the parcel. A balance still open comes out of your proceeds, which hands the buyer a parcel with nothing owing. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. Copies of a recorded deed are available in the deed room at the courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?
faqs.a: The commissioner's general information page says November 15 each year. The site's FAQ still names a December date for the 2024 tax year, so go by the bill in your hands.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

faqs.q: Does Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?
faqs.a: Yes, once granted it renews each year unless the owner changes residence, ownership, or seeks a different exemption. A new buyer has to apply again after a sale.

faqs.q: What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is charged monthly, and a penalty layer stacks on after four months. Its ceiling is one fifth of the tax, so a long-ignored Dallas-area bill grows quickly.
